usage:
EQLMaker {V} - from a running legacy application to a specification, a web application and comparison tests

  eqlmaker init [folder]                      create a project folder with eqlmaker.json
  eqlmaker record --scenario <file.json>      run a scenario and record it
  eqlmaker record --start [--name n] [--no-video]   record while a person works; end with: eqlmaker record --stop
  eqlmaker reset                              undo what an aborted capture left on the database server
  eqlmaker correlate <recording>              time line: chapters -> actions -> statements -> tables
  eqlmaker spec <recording> [...]             specification of masks, queries and tables from time lines
  eqlmaker read <files|folders> [--reader name]   read the files of the application (PowerBuilder libraries): menus, windows, SQL
  eqlmaker export-sql <recording>             statements of a recording as table sql.tsv (for tools that replay statements)
  eqlmaker convert-scenario <file.json>       convert a scenario file of the earlier recorder
  eqlmaker manual <file>                      take over a manual (PDF, HTML, DOCX, TXT, Markdown) as project context
  eqlmaker generate [--template name]         guided step: workspace and instructions for the new web application
  eqlmaker clone [--renderer name]            guided step: workspace and instructions for the read-only 1:1 clone
  eqlmaker video <recording A> <recording B>  two recordings side by side on one time axis, with player page
  eqlmaker verify screens <A> <B>             compare pictures (folders or files)
  eqlmaker verify db <recording A> <recording B>   compare the measured database changes of two recordings
  eqlmaker video-import <file.mp4>            read time stamps, transcript and key frames of a narrated video; findings
  eqlmaker narrate-draft <captions> [--video f] [--lang de]   narration script from the caption timeline of a video
  eqlmaker narrate --video <f> --script <f> --voice <id> --out <f> [--music f --music-volume 30]   spoken narration (Fish Speech)
  eqlmaker enrich [--finish]                  guided step: take findings over into the web application, with report
  eqlmaker import-log <file>                  turn a server log written earlier into a recording with events only
  eqlmaker clock                              clock of the database server minus the clock of this machine
  eqlmaker web-shot <url> <file.png>          picture of a web page from a browser without a window
  eqlmaker sample [--flaw] [--no-video]       the whole pipeline with the sample application
  eqlmaker selftest                           check tools, database and the sample run
  eqlmaker mcp                                MCP server on standard input/output
  eqlmaker windows | controls <title>         list windows / the controls of a window
  eqlmaker background-run <desktop> <command...>   run a command on a separate desktop that is never shown
  eqlmaker version

Common options: --project <folder> (default: current folder), --json (machine-readable result), --lang en|de
Documentation: docs/ in the repository or the package.
mcp.instructions: EQLMaker: operate a Windows program or a web page, record what happens on the screen and in the database, and turn the recording step by step into a specification, a web application and comparison tests. Remote control: take a screenshot first (or list_controls); coordinates are relative to the window chosen with focus_window. Start record_start before launching the application so its database access is captured. Pipeline: record -> correlate -> spec -> generate / clone -> video -> verify; manual_import, video_import and enrich add knowledge from a manual and from a narrated video. generate, clone and enrich are guided steps: the tool prepares a workspace and instructions, you do the work, verify checks the result.
tool.list_windows: Lists the visible top-level windows (title, process, pid, position, size).
tool.focus_window: Makes a window the current window: later coordinates are relative to its top-left corner. Title pattern with * and ?, or pid:<n> / process:<name>. In real mode the window comes to the foreground.
tool.focus_window.title: window title pattern
tool.use_screen: Clears the current window: coordinates are screen coordinates again (real mode).
tool.set_input_mode: Chooses how programs are operated: 'real' (mouse, keyboard and screen; needs a visible desktop) or 'background' (window messages and window pictures; nothing visible moves, limited to programs that react to posted messages).
tool.list_controls: Lists the controls (child windows) of the current window with text, window class and position: a simple view of the structure of a mask.
tool.screenshot: Picture of the current window (or the screen / the web page) as PNG.
tool.screenshot.max_width: scale down to this width (default 1280, 0 = original)
tool.screenshot.screen: whole screen instead of the current window (real mode)
tool.click: Clicks at x,y (relative to the current window, or the screen).
tool.click_control: Clicks a control of the current window found by its text and/or window class (* and ? wildcards).
tool.fill_control: Clicks an edit control found by text/class/index and replaces its content.
tool.move: Moves the mouse visibly to x,y (real mode).
tool.type_text: Types text into the focused control.
tool.type_text.secret: do not write the text into the recording
tool.press_keys: Sends keys in SendKeys syntax: {ENTER}, {TAB}, {F5}, {DEL}; in real mode also ^a (Ctrl+A), %{F4} (Alt+F4), +{TAB} (Shift+Tab).
tool.web_open: Opens a URL in Microsoft Edge or Chrome under remote control (DevTools port 9333, own profile) and makes the page the current target. In background mode the browser runs without a window.
tool.web_click: Finds an element in the web page and clicks it.
tool.web_click.text: exact visible text of the element
tool.web_fill: Clicks into a field of the web page and types a value.
tool.web_eval: Evaluates JavaScript in the web page and returns the result (JSON).
tool.record_start: Starts a recording: actions, database events of the roles/databases named in the configuration (new sessions: start the application after this call), optional video and reference pictures.
tool.record_start.name: name of the recording (folder name)
tool.record_start.region: real mode: workarea (default), screen, x,y,w,h or a window title pattern
tool.record_start.capture_roles: comma-separated login roles to capture instead of the configuration
tool.record_start.capture_databases: comma-separated databases to capture instead of the configuration
tool.record_caption: Sets a chapter mark with a caption at the current time of the recording. Use one chapter per mask or business step.
tool.record_caption.caption: caption
tool.record_stop: Stops the recording and writes the recording folder (recording.json, actions.jsonl, events.jsonl, video.mp4, viewer.html, shots).
tool.run_scenario: Runs a scenario file (JSON steps) and records it.
tool.run_scenario.name: name of the recording
tool.correlate: Pipeline step 2. Builds the time line of a recording by fixed rules: chapters -> actions -> statements -> transactions -> tables. Writes timeline.json into the recording folder.
tool.spec: Pipeline step 3. Derives the specification (steps, masks, statement shapes, tables read and written, links to the manual) from the time lines by fixed rules. Writes spec/spec.json and spec/spec.md.
tool.spec.recordings: comma-separated recordings (default: all of the project)
tool.read_application: Reads the files of the original application (built in: PowerBuilder libraries .pbd/.pbl; others through reader plugins) and writes menus, windows, labels, SQL statements and the tables they use to static/<reader>/reader.json; 'spec' takes the result over. The files are only read.
tool.read_application.paths: comma-separated files or folders of the application, in the order of its library list
tool.read_application.bundle: comma-separated start objects for bundles (what an object uses)
tool.export_sql: Writes the statements of a recording as a tab-separated table (sql.tsv): offset, time, session, user, database, application, kind, statement. Kinds tsql-batch and tsql-rpc are statements that came through the statement trace of the server.
tool.export_sql.out: file to write (default: sql.tsv in the recording folder)
tool.manual_import: Takes the manual of the original program over as project context (PDF, HTML, DOCX, TXT, Markdown): text and chapters; 'spec' links chapters to masks and steps.
tool.manual_import.name: name in the project (default: file name)
tool.generate: Pipeline step 4, a guided step: prepares the folder 'web' from a web template, puts the specification next to it and returns the instructions. You build the application; verify_db checks it. Not an automatic generator.
tool.generate.force: copy the template over an existing folder
tool.clone: Pipeline step 5, a guided step: prepares the folder 'clone' for the read-only 1:1 archive: reference picture and scaffold page per mask, read-only server, instructions. You fill the pages; verify_screens checks them. Not an automatic generator.
tool.clone.force: prepare again over an existing folder
tool.video: Pipeline step 6. Puts two recordings of the same steps (same chapter captions) on one time axis: player page and, with FFmpeg, one combined video.
tool.verify_db: Pipeline step 7. Compares the measured database changes of two recordings of the same steps (original and rebuilt application), step by step. 'equal' only when every changed row agrees.
tool.verify_db.ignore: comma-separated columns to leave out, e.g. invoice.updated_at or *.changed
tool.verify_db.keys: comma-separated key columns whose new values are compared by order of creation (default *.id)
tool.verify_screens: Pipeline step 7. Compares two pictures or two folders of pictures (paired by file name) pixel by pixel; writes a picture of the differences.
tool.verify_screens.tolerance: difference per colour channel that still counts as equal (default 16)
tool.verify_screens.max_percent: share of differing pixels that still passes (default 0.5)
tool.web_shot: Takes a picture of a web page at a given size with a browser that runs without a window (for verify_screens).
tool.video_import: Imports a narrated screen recording (MP4) that shows the time stamp strip: reads the time of the frames, maps video time to wall clock (drift, cuts), transcribes the sound, finds key frames, matches everything to the database events and writes findings per operation.
tool.video_import.recordings: comma-separated recordings whose events belong to the video (default: all)
tool.video_import.transcript: transcript file (VTT, SRT, JSON) instead of speech recognition
tool.video_import.language: language of the speech: auto (default), en, de, ...
tool.video_import.clock_offset_ms: clock of the database server minus clock of the recording machine, when known
tool.video_import.estimate_offset: estimate that offset from the data
tool.enrich: A guided step: starts taking the findings of video_import over into the web application. Remembers the state before (files, and the database comparison when two recordings are named) and returns the instructions with every finding. You decide and change; enrich_decide records, enrich_finish reports.
tool.enrich.findings: name of the findings (default: the only one)
tool.enrich.a: recording of the original, for the comparison before
tool.enrich.b: recording of the web application, for the comparison before
tool.enrich_decide: Records the decision for one finding: adopted (the web application was changed), rejected (not relevant) or open (relevant, cannot be done yet), each with a reason.
tool.enrich_decide.finding: id of the finding, e.g. f3
tool.enrich_decide.note: what was changed and where, or why not
tool.enrich_decide.files: comma-separated files of the web application that were changed
tool.enrich_finish: Ends the enrich step: lists the files of the web application that changed, runs the database comparison after (name the original recording and the new recording of the changed application) and writes the report: every finding adopted, rejected or open with its reason.
tool.enrich_finish.b: new recording of the changed web application
tool.narrate_draft: Prepares a narration script for a finished video from its caption timeline (SRT, WebVTT, whisper JSON or JSON segments): timed segments with a hint and a character budget each. Write the spoken text of every segment into 'text' (at most budget_chars), then call narrate.
tool.narrate_draft.language: language of the narration: de, en, ...
tool.narrate_draft.chars_per_second: speaking rate of the voice in characters per second (default 14)
tool.narrate_draft.out: script file to write (default: next to the captions)
tool.narrate: Lays a spoken narration over a video: speaks every segment of the narration script with a local Fish Speech server and a registered voice reference, fits the clips into their segments (speed-up up to max_tempo), mixes optional background music (ducked under the speech) and writes a new video; the picture is copied unchanged. Fails with the segments to shorten when the speech does not fit.
tool.narrate.voice: voice reference id registered on the Fish Speech server
tool.narrate.language: language of the narration (picks narration.voices of eqlmaker.json)
tool.narrate.music: background music (mp3 or wav), looped to the length of the video
tool.narrate.tts_url: address of the Fish Speech server (default http://127.0.0.1:8080)
tool.clock_check: Measures the clock of the database server against the clock of this machine (for video_import).
tool.import_log: Turns a PostgreSQL server log written earlier into a recording with events only (for correlate, spec and video_import after the fact).
tool.import_log.name: name of the recording
tool.import_log.utc_offset_minutes: UTC offset of the log times in minutes (default: this machine)
prompt.generate: Instructions for building the web application from the specification (guided step).
prompt.clone: Instructions for building the read-only 1:1 archive (guided step).
prompt.enrich: Instructions for taking the findings of a narrated video over into the web application (guided step).
msg.recording_started: recording '{0}' started. Start the application now; end with: eqlmaker record --stop
msg.project_created: edit eqlmaker.json (connection, capture.databases), then: eqlmaker record --scenario <file>
